p01.why: In the front view A's forelegs pinch in where they meet the bulging chest, while B's forelegs come down as full, clean columns and show a clearer elbow from the side.

p02.why: The two ankylosaurs look the same in every view; only a few edge pixels differ.

p03.why: The two beetles look the same; the legs differ by a pixel at most.

p04.why: Seen from the top, A's mid-body swells wider (53 vs 50 cm) and steps in sharply at both ends; B tapers more evenly.

p05.why: A's forearms balloon out past a pinched elbow into clubs, while B's arms taper evenly and its hips and thighs are fuller.

p06.why: A's knees bulge out like balls below thin thighs, while B's fuller thighs taper smoothly into the knee.

p07.why: The two small lizards look the same in every view.

p08.why: The two tusked boars look the same; only the outline shifts by a pixel.

p09.why: B's upper legs have muscle mass and taper down to slim shins, while A's legs are thin tubes of even width.

p10.why: The two scorpions look the same in every view.

p11.why: A's body bulges slightly wider behind the neck (47 vs 45 cm); otherwise the two sea serpents match and neither is better.

p12.why: B's thigh is a full drumstick that tapers into the knee, while A's thigh is thinner and flatter.

p13.why: The two bears match in legs, torso and head.

p14.why: B's hind thigh shows creases and faceted folds down its length and above the knee, while A's hind leg is smooth with a clean knee.

p15.why: The two salamanders look the same; B's mid-body is a hair fuller at most.

p16.why: The two ants look the same; only the leg edges move by a pixel.

p17.why: The two goblins look the same; B's thigh and neck are only a hair fuller.

p18.why: The two rearing snakes have the same spindle-shaped raised body and the same head.

p19.why: The two rhinos look the same; B's chest is only fractionally fuller.

p20.why: A has a lumpy hind knee, and in the front view its forelegs kink and pinch under the chest; B's legs are clean columns with a smooth taper.
